paragraphs: Aerodynamic inverse design starts with a desired physical outcome and searches for a shape that achieves it. Searching directly through three-dimensional shapes is difficult because the space of possibilities is enormous. The paper targets approaches that simplify this problem through two-dimensional projections or modifications of existing shapes, restricting the designs they can explore.

3DID learns a compact, continuous representation that combines geometry with physical field information. Optimization therefore operates in a space that represents both what a shape looks like and its associated physics. Its first stage uses a diffusion sampler guided by gradients to explore this space broadly and produce candidate designs.

A second stage refines each candidate toward the objective while preserving its topology. This separates broad exploration from detailed improvement, supporting direct three-dimensional design from scratch. The authors report high-fidelity geometries and better solution quality and design versatility than existing methods. The contribution is a way to connect learned physical information with both stages of the design search.
neurips-2025-3did-direct-3d-inverse-desi.tldr: 3DID combines a learned physics–geometry representation with broad search and topology-preserving refinement to improve direct three-dimensional aerodynamic design.

paragraphs: Vehicles can improve their understanding of nearby traffic by sharing sensor observations, especially when objects are hidden from one viewpoint. Aerial observations offer another perspective, but the authors identify a shortage of real-world data for studying cooperation between vehicles and drones. AGC-Drive supplies a dataset specifically for this setting.

The collection platform combines two vehicles, each carrying five cameras and a LiDAR sensor, with a drone carrying a forward-facing camera and LiDAR. The dataset includes approximately 80,000 LiDAR frames and 360,000 images across 14 driving scenarios. Its 350 scenes have annotated three-dimensional bounding boxes covering 13 object categories, and 17% of the data involves dynamic interactions.

The paper also provides benchmarks for vehicle-to-vehicle and vehicle-to-drone perception, allowing both collaboration settings to be studied. Supporting tools address alignment across time and space, visualization, and collaborative annotation. Together, these resources make aerial-ground perception more accessible to research; the abstract presents the dataset and evaluation infrastructure rather than a measured improvement from a particular perception model.
neurips-2025-agc-drive-a-large-scale-dat.tldr: AGC-Drive provides real-world vehicle and drone sensor data, annotations, benchmarks, and tools for studying collaborative three-dimensional perception.

paragraphs: Blockchain transactions mix specialized symbols, ordinary text, and numerical values. That mixture makes their structure different from the text usually processed by language models. BlockScan addresses anomaly detection by designing a Transformer around transaction data, rather than relying on fixed detection rules or applying an existing language model directly.

The system begins with a modular tokenizer that handles the different input types while balancing their information. It then uses a customized masked language modeling objective for pretraining. RoPE embeddings and FlashAttention support longer sequences. A separate detection method converts model outputs into anomaly decisions, and the paper provides theoretical analysis of that method.

Evaluations on Ethereum and Solana report strong anomaly detection while keeping false positives low. In the reported Solana comparison, BlockScan was the only evaluated method to detect anomalous transactions with high accuracy; alternatives had very low or zero recall. The results support the value of adapting tokenization, pretraining, and detection together to the structure of blockchain transactions.
neurips-2025-blockscan-detecting-anomali.tldr: BlockScan adapts Transformer tokenization, pretraining, and detection to blockchain transactions, reporting strong anomaly detection on Ethereum and Solana.

paragraphs: A parametric CAD object has both a visible shape and a construction sequence that produces it. Editing the shape therefore requires appropriate changes to that sequence. CADMorph addresses three linked requirements: retaining the original sequence structure, making valid parameter edits, and matching the desired geometry, despite scarce examples of complete editing tasks.

The framework coordinates two pretrained models in an iterative loop. During planning, attention maps from a parameter-to-shape diffusion model identify sequence segments to change. A masked-parameter model fills those segments with candidate edits. During verification, the parameter-to-shape model represents each candidate in a shape space and selects the one closest to the target.

This division gives each stage a concrete responsibility while drawing on geometric and design knowledge already learned by the models. Both models are trained without editing triplets, addressing the stated data bottleneck. The authors report improvements over GPT-4o and specialized CAD baselines, along with applications to repeated editing and reverse-engineering enhancement.
neurips-2025-cadmorph-geometrydriven-par.tldr: CADMorph edits parametric CAD sequences through a plan–generate–verify loop using pretrained models that do not require editing-triplet training data.

paragraphs: Very long inputs create a tension between retaining useful information and keeping memory costs manageable. Compression methods can lose details, while methods that preserve extensive random access require substantial memory. REFORM addresses this tension with an inference framework that combines compact processing of the full input with selective reconstruction of relevant information.

In its first phase, REFORM reads input chunks incrementally, maintains a compressed key-value cache, and builds context representations across model layers. It also uses early exit to improve efficiency. In the second phase, similarity matching identifies important tokens, gathers them, and selectively recomputes their key-value representations for subsequent processing.

At a context length of one million, the authors report performance gains exceeding 50% on RULER and 27% on BABILong relative to baselines. They also report improvements on three additional benchmarks, alongside 30% lower inference time and 5% lower peak memory usage. These findings support combining compression with targeted recomputation to improve both information use and computational efficiency.
neurips-2025-compress-gather-and-recompu.tldr: REFORM processes long inputs through compression and selective recomputation, reporting improved benchmark performance with lower inference time and peak memory.

paragraphs: Turning a natural-language request into a graph database query requires understanding both the request and the database structure. Selecting the relevant schema is therefore an important part of producing correct Cypher. Cypher-RI makes this selection part of the model's reasoning process, connecting it directly to query generation throughout the pipeline.

The framework uses reinforcement learning to train this integrated behavior. Textual context guides schema selection, and the selected schema feeds back into subsequent reasoning. This recursive relationship matters because decisions about which parts of the database are relevant can shape how the request is interpreted and expressed as a query.

The authors evaluate a seven-billion-parameter model trained with this approach and report stronger performance than the compared baselines. On CypherBench, they report a 9.41% accuracy improvement over GPT-4o. The finding supports incorporating schema selection into learned reasoning for Text-to-Cypher, with the reported advantage specifically demonstrated in the benchmark comparison described by the paper.
neurips-2025-cypher-ri-reinforcement-lea.tldr: Cypher-RI uses reinforcement learning to integrate schema selection into query reasoning, improving Text-to-Cypher accuracy on CypherBench.

paragraphs: Graph-based nearest-neighbor methods connect dataset items and search those connections for points close to a query. Popular systems use beam search to maintain promising candidates during exploration. This paper focuses on when that exploration should stop, replacing a commonly used beam-width-based stopping condition with one based on distances.

The resulting Adaptive Beam Search has a theoretical guarantee under a stated condition: the search graph must be navigable. When that condition holds, the method approximately solves the nearest-neighbor problem. This establishes a connection between a graph's navigability and the accuracy of search, giving the stopping rule a formal foundation.

The authors also test the rule on navigable graphs and on approximately navigable structures used in practice, including HNSW and Vamana. Across the evaluated recall levels, datasets, graph constructions, and requested neighbor counts, it outperforms standard beam search. The practical results extend beyond the exact theoretical setting, while the formal guarantee remains conditional on graph navigability.
neurips-2025-distance-adaptive-beam-sear.tldr: A distance-based stopping rule improves graph nearest-neighbor search empirically and guarantees approximate accuracy when the graph is navigable.

paragraphs: Low-rank recurrent neural networks can model how neural systems perform cognitive tasks, but fitting them efficiently and interpreting their behavior remain challenging. This paper studies teacher-training settings through the neural engineering framework, which treats a network as an approximation to a target differential equation built from random nonlinear basis functions.

That perspective connects representational capacity to the activation function and parameter distribution. The authors adapt it for online training, reporting better performance with much smaller networks than FORCE and improvements over similarly sized backpropagation-trained networks with substantially less training time. They also extend orthogonal matching pursuit to seek the smallest network approximating a given dynamical system.

At the opposite size extreme, infinite-unit low-rank networks converge to a Gaussian process over differential equations. This connection supports optimizing parameter distributions through marginal likelihood; the associated covariance has a closed form for particular nonlinearities. The authors report benefits even for finite networks and introduce active learning that accelerates training by selecting especially informative activity patterns.
neurips-2025-efficient-training-of-minim.tldr: The paper develops efficient low-rank RNN training through differential-equation approximation, compact network selection, Gaussian-process connections, and active learning.

paragraphs: Grouped Relative Policy Optimization learns from reward differences among responses to the same input. For vision-language models, the authors observe that these rewards often become similar as training progresses. The resulting weak gradient signal can cause improvements in step-by-step reasoning to stall or collapse, motivating training questions that evolve with the model.

EvolvedGRPO progressively edits instructions to make questions more challenging as capabilities improve. Its two editing strategies span visual and textual modalities, using increasingly demanding instructions and reinforcement-learning-based adversarial data augmentation. To handle questions that are initially too difficult, training begins with simpler subproblems and increases their difficulty over time.

This progression enables prefix-style process rewards alongside group-relative rewards, combining feedback about intermediate reasoning with comparisons among responses. The authors report state-of-the-art multimodal reasoning performance among open-source reinforcement-learning models, approaching GPT-4o, plus stronger performance on unseen general vision-language benchmarks. The findings support adapting question difficulty throughout training to sustain useful learning signals.
neurips-2025-evolvedgrpo-unlocking-reaso.tldr: EvolvedGRPO progressively adjusts multimodal question difficulty to sustain reinforcement-learning signals and improve vision-language reasoning.

paragraphs: Finetuning is commonly viewed as dependable for teaching response styles but unreliable for teaching facts. This paper questions whether that distinction explains the observed outcomes. The authors conduct a large experimental study with the Gemini v1.5 family, using deliberately constructed datasets that span conditions where finetuning works well and conditions where it struggles.

The study identifies several more specific factors. Question-and-answer training formats produce much stronger knowledge generalization than document-style formats. Numerical information can be harder to retain than categorical information. Models also struggle to use newly learned knowledge in multistep reasoning, even when their training includes similar examples and controls account for augmentation and information volume.

These findings explain why knowledge injection can be difficult without treating factual information as inherently unsuitable for finetuning. The experiments also indicate that learning information about a real event is not fundamentally harder than learning information about writing style. The practical implication is to evaluate data format, information type, and required reasoning together when assessing what finetuning can accomplish.
neurips-2025-from-style-to-facts-mapping.tldr: Finetuning outcomes depend on training format, information type, and reasoning demands more concretely than on a simple distinction between style and facts.

paragraphs: Circuit synthesis can change how logic gates are connected while preserving the computation they perform. This makes structural subgraph matching inadequate for finding some functionally related circuit regions. The paper introduces functional subgraph matching: determining whether a specified logic function is present inside a larger circuit despite changes in its visible graph structure.

The proposed framework separates detection from localization. First, it learns functional representations across AIG circuit representations and post-mapping netlists to detect whether the relevant function is present. Second, graph segmentation identifies its fuzzy boundaries. This separation addresses both the existence of a function and the region associated with it.

On ITC99, OpenABCD, and ForgeEDA benchmarks, the authors report an average functional detection accuracy of 93.8% and a boundary-identification Dice score of 91.3%, improving significantly over structural methods. The findings support using learned functional information when synthesis obscures structural similarity, with relevance to the paper's motivating applications in datapath optimization, arithmetic verification, and hardware trojan detection.
neurips-2025-functional-matching-of-logi.tldr: The paper detects and localizes logic functions inside circuits using learned functional representations, overcoming structural changes caused by synthesis.

paragraphs: Gates regulate how much information passes through a neural network, but their specific effects within softmax attention have received less systematic study. This paper compares more than 30 attention variants using 15-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts models and 1.7-billion-parameter dense models trained on a 3.5-trillion-token dataset, examining where and how gating helps.

The central result is that a separate sigmoid gate for each attention head, placed after scaled dot-product attention, consistently improves performance in the experiments. The change also improves training stability, supports larger learning rates, and strengthens scaling behavior. Comparisons across gate placements and computations help isolate the mechanisms associated with these improvements.

The authors attribute the benefits to added nonlinearity in attention's low-rank mapping and sparse gating scores that depend on the query. They report reduced massive activations and attention sinks, along with better long-context extrapolation. The results make a specific architectural recommendation, and the abstract states that the most effective output-gating design is used in Qwen3-Next.
neurips-2025-gated-attention-for-large-l.tldr: Head-specific sigmoid gates after attention improve tested language models through added nonlinearity and query-dependent sparsity.

paragraphs: Sparse autoencoders represent complex internal activations using a small set of learned features, offering a way to study otherwise difficult-to-interpret computations. This paper applies that approach to text-to-image diffusion. It trains autoencoders on the updates made by transformer blocks inside SDXL Turbo's denoising network when the model generates an image in one step.

The learned features transfer without additional training to four-step SDXL Turbo and to the separate, multistep SDXL base model. The authors also find that the features are interpretable and causally affect image generation. This makes them useful for testing how internal computations influence outputs, beyond simply describing patterns in activations.

To evaluate those effects, the paper introduces RIEBench, which tests image edits made during generation by activating or deactivating individual features. The benchmark reveals that different transformer blocks have different strengths across edit categories. Together, the transfer and intervention results establish sparse autoencoders as a promising tool for understanding and manipulating the internal mechanisms of the studied diffusion models.
neurips-2025-one-step-is-enough-sparse-a.tldr: Sparse autoencoders trained on one-step SDXL Turbo reveal controllable features that transfer to four-step Turbo and multistep SDXL without retraining.

paragraphs: An estimate is more useful when accompanied by an uncertainty bound that accurately reflects how wrong it could be. Overly conservative bounds can obscure the quality of an estimator. This paper derives a tight bound for kernel-based estimation that applies to finite data and can accommodate noise that is correlated across observations.

The analysis assumes bounds on the norms of the unknown function and the noise. Within those constraints, it identifies the worst-case function in the chosen hypothesis class at any requested input location. The resulting uncertainty therefore has a precise interpretation tied to the permitted functions and disturbances, rather than relying on an unlimited-data approximation.

The authors show that the worst-case value can be expressed through a Gaussian process posterior mean and covariance when the measurement-noise covariance is chosen optimally. Their theoretical analysis and comparisons with prior results support both tightness and ease of computation. The contribution connects constrained worst-case estimation to Gaussian process quantities while retaining the stated norm-boundedness assumptions.
neurips-2025-optimal-kernel-regression-b.tldr: The paper derives tight finite-data kernel regression uncertainty bounds under norm-bounded function and noise assumptions, including correlated noise.

paragraphs: Offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning trains agents to reach goals using existing trajectories, without further environment interaction. Long tasks remain difficult even with hierarchical policies. The authors identify poor subgoal choices by the high-level policy as a main bottleneck and observe that advantage estimates often have the wrong sign when learning over long horizons.

An advantage estimate indicates whether a choice is better or worse than the value used for comparison. An incorrect sign can therefore give misleading learning guidance. OTA changes temporal-difference value learning to account for temporally extended options, shortening the effective horizon and producing clearer advantage estimates for training the high-level policy.

This approach targets the value estimates that guide subgoal learning, connecting temporal abstraction to a specific source of training error. On OGBench, the authors report strong performance on complex maze-navigation and visual robotic-manipulation tasks. The experiments support the claim that better option-aware value estimates can help hierarchical policies handle long-horizon goals from offline data.
neurips-2025-option-aware-temporally-abs.tldr: OTA incorporates options into value learning to shorten the effective horizon and improve the signals used to learn high-level subgoals.

paragraphs: Retrieval-augmented generation supplies a language model with external evidence, but the model can still produce answers that contradict it. This paper examines cases where retrieved information is relevant and accurate yet conflicts with information stored in model parameters. It investigates how internal computations contribute to that failure to follow the supplied evidence.

The authors identify a subset of feed-forward networks in middle-to-deep layers that are disproportionately active during unfaithful generation. ParamMute suppresses activations in these associated networks and calibrates the model toward retrieved knowledge. The intervention therefore targets the influence of internal parametric information alongside the model's use of external context.

The paper introduces CoFaithfulQA to evaluate conflicts between internal knowledge and accurate external evidence. Across that benchmark and ConFiQA, ParamMute significantly improves faithfulness and reduces reliance on parametric memory. These findings support addressing internal knowledge dominance as part of retrieval-augmented generation, particularly in the evidence-conflict scenarios that motivate the method and its evaluation.
neurips-2025-parammute-suppressing-knowl.tldr: ParamMute suppresses feed-forward networks associated with unfaithful answers to help language models follow accurate retrieved evidence.

paragraphs: A vision-language model may receive individually safe images and prompts yet produce unsafe content from their combination. This paper investigates that compositional failure, extending attention beyond specially crafted malicious images. The authors connect it to broad reasoning capabilities and a safety snowball effect, in which responses become progressively more harmful over an interaction.

Their Safety Snowball Agent framework uses autonomous agents and tools to study this behavior. At a high level, it first obtains an initial response using generated or retrieved imagery, then refines subsequent prompts to intensify unsafe outputs. The framework tests how the evolving interaction can turn otherwise safe visual material into part of a jailbreak.

The experiments report high jailbreak success rates against the evaluated vision-language models and show that nearly any image can be used in the tested process. The authors interpret this as a challenge rooted in general model capabilities. The safety implication is that evaluating individual inputs alone can miss risks created by combinations and the progression of a conversation.
neurips-2025-safe-safe-unsafe-exploring-.tldr: The paper shows how combinations of safe visual inputs and evolving prompts can elicit unsafe outputs from vision-language models.

paragraphs: Spreadsheets contain formulas and structural relationships that ordinary table datasets often do not capture. Sheetpedia assembles more than 290,000 spreadsheets from over 324,000 workbooks to support research on those features. Its sources include enterprise email archives, an existing web corpus, and a new collection from Excel discussion forums.

The collection pipeline standardizes formats, filters languages, and removes duplicates. The corpus includes real formulas and annotations, with more than 78% English content. This emphasis matters because spreadsheet understanding requires interpreting how cells and formulas work together, alongside reading the values or text that appear in a table.

The authors demonstrate usefulness by finetuning language models for mapping natural-language requests to semantic ranges and formulas. Using a rejection-sampling strategy to generate training data, their models reach up to 97.5% accuracy on the range task and 71.7% on the formula task, substantially exceeding baselines. The abstract describes public release as planned and positions the corpus as a resource for spreadsheet intelligence.
neurips-2025-sheetpedia-a-300k-spreadshe.tldr: Sheetpedia collects real spreadsheets with formula semantics and supports finetuning models to translate natural language into ranges and formulas.

paragraphs: Text-to-motion models often learn from brief or generic descriptions, limiting how precisely users can specify movement. SnapMoGen addresses this data constraint with motion capture paired with expressive textual annotations. The dataset contains 20,000 clips totaling 44 hours, with descriptions averaging 48 words compared with 12 words in HumanML3D.

The clips retain their original temporal continuity within longer sequences, supporting research on extended motion generation and transitions between movements. Alongside the dataset, the authors introduce MoMask++, which represents motion as token sequences at multiple scales. A single generative masked transformer learns to generate all of those tokens, making better use of the token representation.

MoMask++ achieves state-of-the-art results on HumanML3D and OmniMotion according to the reported evaluations. The authors also demonstrate processing casual user prompts by using a language model to rewrite them into SnapMoGen's descriptive style. The paper therefore contributes both richer supervision for detailed motion requests and a generation method evaluated on established motion benchmarks.
neurips-2025-snapmogen-human-motion-gene.tldr: SnapMoGen pairs motion capture with expressive descriptions, while MoMask++ uses multiscale motion tokens to improve text-driven motion generation.

paragraphs: Using language models for optimization involves translating a problem into a form that can be solved reliably. SolverLLM addresses this by spending additional computation at inference time without further model training. It searches over mathematical formulations and translates them into solver-ready code, making formulation quality a central part of the solution process.

The search builds on Monte Carlo Tree Search with three changes. Dynamic expansion adapts the generation of candidate formulations. Prompt backpropagation carries outcome-based feedback into further exploration. Uncertainty backpropagation accounts for how reliable the reward information is when making search decisions. Together, these mechanisms guide the model's exploration of possible formulations.

Across six standard benchmark datasets, SolverLLM outperforms both prompt-based and learning-based baselines and shows strong generalization without additional training. The findings support investing inference-time effort in guided formulation search. They also connect successful optimization assistance to the model's ability to construct useful mathematical representations and executable solver inputs, rather than only generating a final answer.
neurips-2025-solverllm-leveraging-test-t.tldr: SolverLLM uses inference-time tree search to generate mathematical formulations and solver-ready code, improving optimization results without additional training.

paragraphs: Determining an image's origin involves distinguishing training examples, new model generations, and material from external sources. This paper studies that problem through diffusion trajectories: the changing behavior across the sequence of denoising steps. Its central idea is that the full temporal pattern provides useful evidence for classifying provenance.

The authors show that using dynamics throughout the trajectory supports more robust classification. This challenges the conjecture that membership inference is effective only within a narrow range of denoising stages. They also find that representative membership-inference methods fail under distribution shifts or when model-generated images are included, exposing problems with existing evaluation practices.

For identifying the generating model, the paper presents what the authors describe as the first white-box attribution approach directly applicable to diffusion. That access setting is part of the stated contribution. Taken together, the results motivate a unified provenance framework that considers training membership, generated outputs, and external images within the same analysis of modern generative systems.
neurips-2025-tracing-the-roots-leveragin.tldr: Full diffusion trajectories improve image-origin analysis and expose weaknesses in membership inference under distribution shifts and generated-data mixtures.

paragraphs: Continual learning asks a model to acquire successive tasks while retaining earlier knowledge. Perturb-and-Merge addresses forgetting by combining the previous model with the model trained on each new task. After each training stage, inference uses a convex combination of their parameters, allowing earlier and newly acquired information to contribute to the resulting model.

The authors analyze total loss increases across tasks and derive a closed-form merging coefficient under mild assumptions. They also identify a regularization term involving the task vector and the loss Hessian that can reduce degradation from merging. This links training behavior to how well the resulting parameters can be combined afterward.

The term can be approximated through second-order symmetric finite differences. A stochastic perturbation along the task-vector direction provides an effective approximation without additional forward or backward passes. The framework also incorporates LoRA to reduce memory overhead. The authors report state-of-the-art results on several continual-learning benchmarks, supporting the combined strategy of preparing models for merging during training and merging before inference.
neurips-2025-train-with-perturbation-inf.tldr: Perturb-and-Merge prepares task models for parameter merging during training, then combines old and new models to reduce continual-learning forgetting.

paragraphs: Fairness interventions often constrain model predictions, while biases can also be embedded in the features used to make those predictions. This paper develops a framework for adjusting data representations directly. Its goal is to manage the relationship between useful predictive information and information associated with sensitive attributes, rather than treating representation choices as fixed.

Using sufficient dimension reduction, the method separates the feature space into target-relevant, sensitive, and shared components. Selectively removing sensitive information provides a way to control the fairness–utility trade-off. Shared components are central because information connected to sensitive attributes can also matter for predicting the target, making removal a consequential choice.

The theoretical analysis tracks how prediction error and fairness gaps change as shared subspaces are added. Influence functions further characterize effects on the asymptotic behavior of parameter estimates. Experiments on synthetic and real-world data support the theoretical insights and show improved fairness while preserving predictive performance, demonstrating the value of analyzing which representation components drive each outcome.
neurips-2025-understanding-fairness-and-.tldr: The paper decomposes data representations into predictive, sensitive, and shared components to analyze and manage fairness–accuracy trade-offs.

paragraphs: Local SGD reduces communication during distributed training by allowing workers to perform local optimization before combining their updates. The combined update then passes through an outer optimizer to produce a new shared model. This paper studies that outer step, whose learning rate and optimizer choices are less understood than the local training settings.

The authors prove convergence guarantees showing that tuning the outer learning rate can balance optimization error against stochastic gradient noise. It can also compensate for poorly tuned inner learning rates. Their theory indicates that an outer learning rate greater than one can sometimes be appropriate, making the outer step an important tuning decision.

The analysis extends to outer momentum and includes a new data-dependent treatment that provides further insight into learning-rate selection. Experiments with standard language models and several outer optimizers validate the theoretical findings. The contribution clarifies how local training and global updating interact, while preserving the conditional nature of the recommendation to use larger-than-one outer learning rates.
neurips-2025-understanding-outer-optimiz.tldr: The paper shows how Local SGD's outer learning rate balances error and noise, compensates for inner-rate mistuning, and can sometimes exceed one.

paragraphs: Video prediction requires tracking nearby changes while retaining information from earlier frames. Global attention becomes expensive for large, long sequences, while convolutional and recurrent approaches can lose long-range information. VideoTitans adapts gradient-driven Titans memory from language modeling to video prediction, combining a limited attention window with mechanisms for retaining longer-term information.

Its attention core uses a sliding window and scales linearly with sequence length and spatial resolution. An episodic memory retains informative tokens using a gradient-based surprise signal. A small collection of persistent tokens encodes task-specific prior information to stabilize training and improve generalization. These components provide distinct ways to use recent observations, selected past information, and learned task knowledge.

Experiments on Moving-MNIST, Human3.6M, TrafficBJ, and WeatherBench report consistently fewer floating-point operations and competitive visual fidelity against recurrent, convolutional, and efficient-transformer methods. Ablations find significant contributions from each component. The results support this combination of attention and memory as an efficient video-prediction architecture, with competitive rather than universally superior visual quality.
neurips-2025-videotitans-scalable-video-.tldr: VideoTitans combines local attention, surprise-driven memory, and persistent task tokens to reduce video-prediction computation while maintaining competitive visual fidelity.
